books.section: Topic 6.10 Development of the Middle Class
The Rise of the Modern American City

primary_sources: Electric streetcars on Canal Street, New Orleans, Detroit Publishing Company postcard, 1907

stimulus.text: The image is a hand-colored postcard of Canal Street, New Orleans, copyrighted 1907 by the Detroit Publishing Company. It shows a wide city street with several sets of streetcar tracks running down its middle and three electric streetcars carrying passengers. Tall commercial buildings line both sides of the street, and a horse-drawn carriage stands at the right edge.
stimulus.source_note: Electric streetcars on Canal Street, New Orleans, 1907 postcard view (Detroit Publishing Company). Public domain image from Wikimedia Commons; viewed by the writer.

stem: The postcard is copyrighted 1907, nearly a decade after Period 6 ends. A historian using it as evidence about streetcars in the 1890s should keep in mind that

options.text: electric streetcars did not exist before 1907
options.misconception: Electric streetcars spread in the 1880s and 1890s, before this postcard.

options.text: the postcard proves that suburbs did not exist anywhere at all in the 1890s
options.misconception: A 1907 street scene proves nothing about whether suburbs existed earlier.

options.text: no one rode streetcars in the 1890s
options.misconception: Streetcars carried city passengers through the 1890s.

options.text: it shows 1890s streetcars, but its 1907 date cannot prove an 1890 street

rationales.A: The first successful electric street railway opened in Richmond in 1888. The cars predate the postcard by years.
rationales.B: Streetcar suburbs grew in the 1880s and 1890s. A later postcard cannot disprove them.
rationales.C: City passengers rode streetcars all through the 1890s.
rationales.D: The cars in the picture are the same kind that spread in the 1880s and 1890s, but a 1907 view cannot by itself prove an 1890 street scene.
rationales.general:
Use the date to set the source's reach.
1. The postcard is copyrighted 1907, after the period ends.
2. Background from the books: electric streetcars spread in the 1880s and 1890s, so the cars themselves fit the period.
3. But the street scene is from 1907, not 1890.
4. So the card shows the technology, not a dated picture of an 1890 street.
Remember: a source proves its own time first; earlier times need earlier evidence.
